findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed that the temperatures from multiple coolers on the cook-line were too high. Since they were in the middle of their lunch rush, we waited approximately 30 minutes after advising cook staff to keep covers closed on coolers to re-probe food. Some food items chilled to an appropriate temperature in that time. The food items that were still too hot are listed below : 
1. Dairy-based sauces (53F) - Broiler prep cooler top
2. Mayo (52F) - Broiler prep cooler top
3. Cut tomatoes (49F) - Broiler prep cooler top
4. Cut lettuce (50F) - Broiler prep cooler top
5. Bleu cheese (50F) - Broiler prep cooler top
6. Whipped cream (54F) - Dessert prep cooler
7. Chicken (50F) - Dessert prep cooler

All food items listed above were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. The broiler prep cooler was directly across from multiple operating broilers, and the area was very hot. Advised PIC to swap from temperature control to time as a control for time/temperature control (TCS) foods in that cooler. Cook staff already have an effective time keeping system in place for time as a control monitoring/labeling. Items in dessert cooler were advised to be placed in another cooler that holds temp more effectively, as those two food items are the only TCS foods stored there. The bottom of both coolers were well cooled (~35F), so advised cook staff to keep covers on cooler tops closed as frequently as possible to retain refrigeration. Inspector will perform a spot-check on 2/26/25 to ensure time as a control is being implemented correctly and remaining TCS foods in coolers are being maintained at the appropriate temperatures (less than 41F).

findings.citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) Observed Madera sauce and BBQ sauce, both house made, to be on the sauce rail at room temperature. Sauces were in the 60°F range. Observed whipped butter on the wait line to be 65F. When a maximum time period of 6 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from temperature control and the FOOD temperature may not exceed 70°F during the 6 hours. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Time tag was placed on the sauces and butter in question. Reference 3-501.19. Switching to cold holding for sauces. Butter will be held with time as contol.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) Finito is stored behind the bar above bottles of liquor and sugar cubes. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on walls behind the ice maker, wall to the right of the prep line, bottom shelf of bar prep cooler, vita mix at bar, speed rail at bar, and walls at the dish room. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Salt and pepper used to fill bottles which is stored in the wait area is not marked. 750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. The bottles were marked.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed tomato, basil and oil mixture on the prep top with no time marking. Also both grill prep rails are holding foods that should be temperature controlled for safety at room temperature. Place time control marks on these items or use temperature to safely hold house made items. 750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

Observed soup and sauce (chipolte mayo) in the walk in cooler with no 7 day date marking. Properly date mark all items in the cooler. Items were discarded. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: Observed Lobster bisque soup on the wait line to be 125F. Hold foods at proper temperatures at all times. Make certain to stir soups regularly to maintain their temperature.  750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: Observed house made sauces to be above 41F in the tops of the prep coolers. These sauces are made and not cooled before being placed into the prep tops. Cool foods so that the prep tops can hold food properly. These items were time marked and will be used or discarded in 4 hours. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Thermometers were missing from the line equipment. Provide thermometers to all units. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment: Observed an employee place sauce from a back stock container into a partially used squeeze bottle. The bottles have not date marking because they are supposed to be fresh daily. Prepare fresh bottles daily. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Observed a squeeze bottle with bbq sauce to be repaired with duct tape. The tape was covering a hole in the bottle. The bottle was discarded in the garbage. Observed a drink with no lid or straw to be stored over the prep area.  Drink was discarded. Properly protect foods. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Upon arrival observed a bin of seasoned flour on the floor. The container was removed promptly before anything could be said. 750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: Observed the sinks being set up to do dishes. The sinks were soiled. Lettuce was observed in the sanitize portion of the sink. 750-820d Sinks shall be cleaned prior to use. Clean sinks prior to set up for dish washing and any time the become soiled between uses.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed that the 3 part sink does not have sanitizer provided to it. The manager is going to use other sanitizer until the dispenser can be repaired. The 3 part sink was in use upon arrival. 750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The top of the dish machine is soiled and holding soiled rags. The rags were removed. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment: Observed garbage cans in the facility to be heavily soiled. Clean containers and maintain clean. 750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily clean able, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers which are maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the small prep cooler to be holding sauces and carmelized onion at 47F Butter in the bottom probed at 46.6F in the middle of the bottom stick. Discard these sauces. 
Observed the batter station at 67F. Ice baths were not properly consturcted. Use ice around all 5 sides of the container at or above the level of the food. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Lemons which have been cleaned and used for zest are observed to have been put back into the box of unwashed lemons.  Store clean food in proper, clean, containers. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer concentraion in the 3 part and all wiping cloth buckets to be 100ppm or less. The dispenser is not functioning properly. Take care to use test strips and ensure that the equipment is funcitonal at least once daily. We are switching to chlorine sanitizer until the chemical company can return to repair the dispenser. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed the drain board (on the clean side) of the dish machine to be soiled with accumulated food debris. Maintain this area clean as to not contaminate the clean dishes and utensils that come out onto this side. Observed clean sheet trays and cutting boards to be on the bottom shelf of a cart that is heavily soiled with mold. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: The floor in the dish area is soiled with a considerable accumulation of water. Repair this area so that the floor does not flood. 750-1100(b) Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed cutting boards on the prep line with scores which are soiled. Also observed a clear food scoop type utensil with a crack and tongs that have a plastic coat which was peeling. Scoop and tongs were discarded. Cutting boards will be replaced or repaired. 750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleansable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed two soiled clear plastic scoops to be stored as clean.  One scoop discarded one was moved to dish. Also observed some soil in the soda guns at the bar. The soda guns were cleaned. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed clean plates to be stored under a sink where there is a drain line. Do not store clean equipment or utensils under drain lines. The plates were moved. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: Faucet at the salad prep sinks leak and are difficult if not impossible to turn off. Repair this sink so that the faucet does not continually drip water. 750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed walls behind the prep line coolers and wall behind the ice machine to be soled with food splash and dust. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
Observed the hand sinks throughout the facility to have caulk lines that are broken, soiled and no longer easily cleansable. Also the caulk line at the splash guards along the rims of the sinks are missing. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: 750-140(a) Observed thermometers to be missing from multiple low boy coolers on the prep line. Thermometers shall be conspicuously placed in all coolers storing TCS foods. Facility management states that thermometer will be replaced during inventory today.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed personal drinks stored in the small reach in cooler on the expo line and on the shelving units in the dry storage area. Facility has a personal drink policy that requires drinks to be labeled and stored in a manner to prevent potential contamination (such as in the speed rail). Food employees shall follow facility's policies regarding personal drink storage. Personal drinks were removed during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the ice cream scoop dipper well with what appears to be a slimy residue and 2) the interior of a knife cover with what appeared to be mold. Food contact surfaces shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use to prevent potential contamination of food. Dipper well was cleaned during inspection. The knife cover was discarded and replaced to correct the violation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800(d) Observed the speed rack holding clean cutting boards in the kitchen to be soiled with food debris and grease. Clean and maintain non-food contact surfaces to prevent potential contamination.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed silver polish stored intermingled with single service articles in the expo area. Single service shall be protected at all times during service. Facility has a policy requiring all potentially toxic substances to be stored in the chemical cage. Food employees shall follow policies regarding chemical storage. Polish was removed and stored in the chemical cage to correct the violation.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the floor under the dish machine and sink at the wine tasting area to be soiled with an accumulation of dust, food debris, and random articles. Floors shall be cleaned and maintained to prevent providing food, water, or harborage for pests.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed on-site prepared sauces and wet batter stored on the cook line at 70-72F. Facility management states that there is no standard operating procedures for cold holding these foods. Time as a public health control (4-hours) should be used for these items. Items should be cold held or time as a control should be used. If time as a control is used, a policy should be developed and provided to SCDPH. TCS foods shall be held at the proper temperatures (41 F or below or 135F or above).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510(a) Observed improper hand washing and poor glove use. (1) Observed food employees put on gloves and handle ready to eat food without properly washing their hands. (2) Observed food employees adjust their hair restraints with their gloves on and return to food handling or food contact surfaces without properly changing their gloves and washing their hands. (3) Observed food employees improperly wash their hands by not using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Proper hand washing and glove use was discussed. Food employees shall wash their hands

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810(b) (1) Observed a wet wiping rag stored on the counter on the expo line. (2) Observed sanitizer buckets at  100 ppm QT on the back prep line. (3) Observed sanitizer buckets at 0 ppm QT at the front expo line and bar. (4) Observed sanitizer buckets mixed with soap and QT on the expo line and at the bar. This is a poor practice. Cease to mix soap and sanitizer. Wet wiping cloths shall be stored in clean sanitizer solution between use. Utilize test strips to ensure that the appropriate concentration of sanitizer is provided.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) (1) Observed a lemon slicer stored soiled with food splash debris at the expo line. (2) Observed the dipping well at the ice cream station to be soiled with dust, soil, and food debris. (3) Observed cutting boards through the prep areas to be generally soiled and scored to the extent that they are no longer easily cleanable.  Clean and maintain food contact surfaces to prevent potential contamination of food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800(e) Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the stand mixer with food debris and 2) the bulk bins on the prep line with food debris. Non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned and maintained.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Observed clear bucket storing clean, sanitized utensils on the back prep line to be soiled with food debris. Clean and rotate storage buckets more frequently to prevent accumulation of debris. Clean, sanitized utensils shall be stored in a manner that prevents potential contamination of food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 Observed the sink at the vegetable prep station to be not shut off completely. Repair faucet to prevent leak from providing water for pests. All plumbing shall be installed and maintained in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code (77 Ill Adm Code 890).

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120(e) (1) Observed no paper towels at the hand washing sink at the bar. (2) Observed the paper towel dispenser at the hand washing sink at the far end of the prep line by the stairs to be non-operational. All hand washing stations shall be supplied with hot water, soap, and a supply of paper towels. Paper towels were provided at these hand washing stations to correct the violation.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 (1) Observed the floor underneath the equipment in the wine tasting area to be soiled with food debris, soil, and random articles. (2) Observed the floor drain at the bar under the 3-compartment sink to be soiled with food debris and random articles. (3) Observed soiled floors in the mop area under the chemical cage;  around the door to dumpster; and throughout the kitchen under and around large equipment and the wall floor juncture to be soiled with food debris and a soil accumulation. Clean and maintain floors to prevent providing food, water, or harborage for pests.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed items that had been cooled in the walk in cooler with no date or time tags. These items are potentially hazardous ready to eat foods. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.  Make sure to time/date tag all TCS foods that are cooled and held in the facility.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed black bean burgers to be at 59F in the prep cooler bottom. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)  Burgers were discarded in the garbage.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed cutting boards throughout the facility that have scores and cracks that are holding food and soil. Observed the back prep table to not be sealed and accumulated with soil at the juncture.  750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleansable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.  Repair or replace cutting boards. Properly clean cutting boards so that they do no accumulate soil.  Clean and seal prep tables so that food debris can not accumulate.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed several wiping cloth buckets with obvious soil accumulation at a temperature below 75F. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions and shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.  SOP for the facility is to change buckets at 90 min intervals. Take care to follow this SOP or change more frequently so that water is not soiled or cold.  Buckets were corrected immediately.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Several hand sinks are separating from the wall. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings. Check hand sinks and replace seals as necessary.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Observed cheese shreds and squeeze sauces (homemade) to be stored on an improper ice bath. Items were probed and found to be holding temperatures in the mid-60s. Discussed using time as a control or creating a proper ice bath. Foods were recently restocked after lunch. Water was added to the ice bath to allow foods to become submerged. Also, observed cold foods on another (similar concern) improper ice bath on the cook line (by fry station). Butters were probed at 74F. Time is going to be used as control on these foods. Labeling is present and easily visible. Indicate the time these foods are placed on the ice bath of the cook line. Use or discard within four hours.

All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 & 153 - A) Butter based sauces in steam table on cook line had surface and internal temperatures of 105F-114F and 126F-130F respectively. Sauces were prepared around 1130a. Manager stated time control is utilized and sauces would be changed out when the new crew starts at 4p. However, the products in question are past the 4hr time frame at that point based on information provided. Also, the labels for foods were marked with AM only and no specific time was indicated for the 4hr time frame for use. Proper labeling of time controlled sauces was discussed. All sauces on the steam table were to be discarded immediately and changed out. 

B) Chipolte sauce in the steam table on the cook line had a surface and internal temperature of 114F and 119F respectively. Cook noted the sauce was changed out around 2p. Sauce was placed on the grill to reheat to 165F prior to being placed back in the steam table for hot holding. Staff were advised the sauce will not hold at 135F/above if double panned in the same manner at beurre blanc sauces. 

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135F/above while on display and service unless time control is being used. When using time as a control, food must be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.160b - Observed an employee touch hat and body without changing gloves. Glove use was discussed and new gloves were donned prior to handling food.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Manager did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to check the temperature of short ribs cooking in the oven. Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed. 

Hands must be properly washed whenever hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - Coating on #10 can opener blade was observed to have chipped away on the end, and a small portion of the coating was loose and starting to fall off at the time of inspection. Manager stated he would place an order for a replacement blade.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750.810b - Observed one of the sani-buckets on the wait line to have cloths stacked over the solution line. Solution was added during the inspection.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) ceiling inside ice machine (mold);   and
B) detachable blades and chopper attachments for the slicer (food debris) - all items taken to dish area to go through ware washing process.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. 
Clean and sanitize the ceiling inside the ice machine and the metal baffle in the bottom as needed to eliminate buildup of mold between full service.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Observed the floor drain cup underneath the dipping well to have fallen aside causing discharging water to pond on the floor. Cup was properly replaced on floor drain during the inspection (the ice cream cooler needed to be moved aside).

Maintain plumbing to prevent ponding water on the floor. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - A) The floor in the far corner of the bar (floor drain under the fruit puree ice baths/ fruit wells) is observed soiled with food debris and bottle caps. There were a few drain flies observed around this floor drain.

B) Floor under the dry storage shelves upstairs were soiled with accumulation of general debris.

C) Floor under the ice machine was soiled with buildup, and the floor drain in front of the machine had an accumulation of water and debris. It was apparent the drain had some buildup in the grate that was not allowing for proper draining. 

Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and drains throughout daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750. 120 - The following foods were observed to be out of temperature on the cook line:
1. vegetable portions stacked above fill line of container in the top of a prep cooler (48F-49F);
2. meatball portions in bottom drawer of a prep cooler (internal temperatures 43F; 49F; 52F; 60F);
3. chicken portions in bottom drawer of salad prep cooler (internal temperatures 45F-47F);   and
4. cheeses and sauces in the top holding area of the broiler prep cooler (internal temperatures 48F).
Coolers used for storage of the aforementioned items did not appear to be failing. Other products in the same coolers were at proper temperature. The broiler cooler appeared to be running warmer due to stacks of portioned cheese slices blocking air flow. Cheese slices that were blocking air vent had internal temperatures of 43F-45F. All of the aforementioned foods were discarded in the trash during inspection. All potentially hazardous foods held in the broiler cooler overnight were discarded in the trash as well. Management will closely monitor temperatures and has made a call to get coolers serviced as well. 

Also, observed the bar cooler holding mainly wine, but also fruit purees, milk, skewers, and juices to be holding temperatures in the 50s. Fruit juice was probed and found to be 51F. Skewers are observed at 52F. Foods that are potentially hazardous were discarded during the inspection. The cooler was made colder during the inspection. The facility struggles with items freezing and manager believed the cooler was just turned too warm without monitoring the temperature. Cooler is not going to be used until the temperature is brought down to 41F. 
Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41F/below or 135F/above)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 & 153 - Butter based sauces in steam table on cook line had surface and internal temperatures of 110F and 116F respectively. Sauces were prepared around 1030a. Management and staff noted time control is utilized, but the time was not documented on the labels at the steam table. Discard time of 2p was placed on the labels.

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135F/above while on display and service unless time control is being used. When using time as a control, food must be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130(d) - Observed plungers and sani-buckets being stored on a shelf over cleaned bulk tubs used to hold cut produce. Manager stated that the produce containers are normally stored on a different shelf. Sani-buckets are observed dripping onto the bottom of the food contact containers. Sani-buckets and plungers were moved during the inspection.

All food and equipment shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510d - Observed an employee dip his hands into sani-water between handling soiled dishes and chemical and then clean dishes. Discussed handwashing with staff and manager. Make sure that employees know to wash hands with soap and water between handling of soiled and clean foods.

To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750.530a - Observed a coffee cup stored on the shelf with sani-buckets and plungers in the dish room over clean equipment. Cup was moved to the soiled side of the dish machine during the inspection. Cease storing personal beverages in such a manner as to potentially cross contaminate equipment and food. Unless the cup has a lid and a straw then employees should wash hands after taking a beverage.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
750.830f - Observed date labels on equipment and utensils after being run through the dish machine. Discussed pulling labels prior to washing or as part of the washing process. Do not restock equipment and utensils with old date labels on them.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A majority of the sani-buckets throughout facility were observed at less than 150ppm. Several buckets were remade and still observed to be at improper concentration. Quat solution was checked at the dispenser/3 part sink and observed to be at 200ppm. All sani-buckets were remade with fresh solution (200ppm). Clean wiping cloths were retrieved and soaked with sanitizer from dispenser prior to placing in sani-buckets.

Maintain quat solution at proper concentration range of 150-400ppm. Make sure solution is allowed to run through the line for several seconds prior to filling buckets, and soak cloths in solution prior to placing sani-buckets (wiping cloths can absorb sanitizer/cause solution to weaken at an accelerated rate).

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - The floor and floor drain underneath the fruit ice well of the bar is observed soiled with food and mold. Clean the drain and the floor. Also. observed the floor underneath the handsink in the tasting bar to be soiled.

Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Observed the mop at the mop sink to be stored with wet head to the ground. Inverted during inspection. Store mop hanging, inverted, or resting over the bucket wringer in order to allow for proper drip drying.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - (R) Documentation of time and date was not present for any of the potentially hazardous foods that were cooked today and were in some stage of the cooling process. Foods included, but were not necessarily limited to, cooked rice, pasta (in walkin cooler and bagged portions in cook line cooler), cooked vegetables and sauces. Management and staff must work on a system for not only documenting the time and date of cooling foods but also tracking the temperature to ensure proper cooling for all cooked potentially hazardous foods. Rice, noodles, and other cooling foods should not be portioned and placed in coolers on the cook line until they have reach at least 41F/below.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. Provide proper labels for cooked/cooling foods.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.250 A) See notes in General Comments. Observed cheese shreds being stored on an improper ice bath. Ice was present, but without water in the bath, the product container only rests on the ice and cools the bottom of the container. Cheese shreds were probed and found to be 49F. Ice was added during the inspection. Cheese shreds are normally changed every shift which is four to five hours.

B) 1. Minced garlic and whipping cream were observed out in the back prep area. Surface temperature of garlic was 74F. Whipping cream had surface and internal temperatures of 68F and 54F respectively. Manager was unsure as out how long products were out in the prep area. Both items were discarded in the trash.
2. Tray of parsnips out on the cook line had a surface temperature of 73F. Manager noted the product was pulled from the walkin cooler for portioning, but the person working on portioning had to leave. Manager was unsure as to how long product was out of cold holding. Parsnips were discarded in the trash.
Do not leave potentially hazardous foods out longer than needed for use. If process is interrupted, then place the foods back in coolers to avoid temperature abuse.

All PHF shall be kept at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - The right portion of the steam table (left side of the cookline) was not holding hot foods at 135F/above. Internal temperatures for sauces were observed at 126F. Sauces in question were removed from steam table to be discarded. Two butter sauces in pans stacked inside another pan on the left side of the same unit had an internal temperature of 130F. Manager stated the butter based sauces have to be maintained at 130F otherwise they break apart. Manager was advised to use time control for the sauces that will not be held at 135F/above due to quality purposes. Label product with time and use or discard w/in 4hrs.
NOTE: Rice and mashed potatoes on the left side of the hot holding unit were at 173F and 171F. Make sure both sides of the steam table are at proper setting to maintain foods at 135F/above. 

All PHF shall be kept at 135F/above while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140(b) - A) Container of Bolognese in ice bath had internal temperature ranging from 68F to +100F. Manager went to check the temperature chart and observed that times and temperatures were not being tracked for any of the products today. Based on information provided Manager thought it was cooling for ~3 hours. Bolognese was placed back on the stove and reheated above 165F prior to being hot held for service. Bolognese was to be held hot until the close of business today, and leftovers will be discarded.
Maintain ice baths to allow for proper/rapid cooling. Use several smaller containers to allow for rapid cooling, and then combine into a larger storage container once foods are properly cooled.

B) Trays of cooked and baked onions and baked tomatoes were observed on a rack next to the stove in the back prep area. Temperatures were at 91F (cooked onions), 71F (baked onions), & 73F (baked tomatoes). Manager was advised cooked vegetables, pasta and all other foods must be cooling in ice baths or in the walkin cooler/freezer. Foods should not be allowed to sit at room temperature for cooling purposes. Trays of foods were placed in the walkin cooler, and temperatures began to rapidly drop.

Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Monitor time and temperature of cooling foods to ensure benchmark temperatures are reached w/in designated time frames. The only way to know foods are cooling properly is to take temperatures and monitor the products during cooling process.
(Educational handout provided)

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
750-280 - A) Observed the handle of the tongs used at the tasting bar to be resting in the baskets of crackers. Discussed proper handling of crackers so that customers are not grabbing the crackers and tongs at the same time. Make sure that the handle of the tongs remains out of direct contact with the food. 

B) Cook was observed preparing blackened salmon appetizer and had a glove on only one hand. Salmon was already on the plate and finishing touches were occurring. Pieces of salmon were being repositioned with hands. Employee was advised to avoid touching salmon with un-gloved hand. A better practice is to have gloves on both hands when working with ready to eat foods.

Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750-510a Observed an employee washing hands and using clean hands to turn off the faucet. Use a barrier when turning off the faucet to avoid contaminating clean hands.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

750-510d Observed an employee using a common towel to dry hands after handwashing. Cease using a common towel to dry hands. Use a proper paper towel.
To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-830 The dish machine at the bar was not properly sanitizing. Super Trump detergent was connected to both the detergent lines and the sanitizing lines. The Super Trump was removed from sanitizing line and proper sanitizing solution was added. The machine had to be primed for over five minutes in order for chemical to be properly drawn through the line. 

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket at south end of cook line tested at ~100ppm quat.

Maintain quat solutions at proper concentration (150-400ppm). Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Ice machine was soiled around opening in ceiling where ice comes out (black mold), on the metal baffle (pink mold around rectangle openings); and in the groove behind the hinge of lower lid (buildup/mold).

Clean and sanitize the ice machine as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - None of the employees on-site at the time of inspection had proof of IL Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification (FSSMC). One person recently promoted to management had proof of ServSafe. Manager with proof of FSSMC arrived during inspection to correct the violation. Management noted some staff are in the process of receiving FSSMCs, and some are in the process of preparing to take the manager certification course.

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Managers.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Mixed vegetables cooling in the walkin cooler had surface temperature of 64F-75F. Time was not marked on the label. Manager noted the vegetables were prepared around 145p. Vegetables were removed from the large container in which they were originally observed (a little less than half full and covered) and were placed on baking sheets with proper labels in the walkin cooler to quickly cool the product.
Several other cooked/cooled foods prepared earlier today (surface temperatures or 43F/below), including but not necessarily limited to chicken breasts, beef, and noodles were not labeled.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. Provide proper labels for cooked/cooling foods.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120(a) - Observed a drawer under the middle preparation cooler to have a fallen piece preventing complete closure of the drawer. Foods within this drawer were probed and found to be in the mid-high fifties (Turkey 59). During the inspection, the adjacent drawer was also found to be effected by the inability to close the adjacent drawer. Employee was able to repair the drawer so that closure was complete. Coopers Hawk conducts temperature checks two times a day. It was determined that the foods were likely at appropriate cold holding temperatures prior to just after lunch. Foods will be used within four hours or discarded.

Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - The right portion of the steam table (left side of the cookline) is not holding hot foods at 135F or above. Butter sauce, au jus, potatoes and cream sauce were all found at temperatures from 119F to 129F. During the inspection, the steam table temperature was increased and foods were discarded (au jus was reheated to 165F).

All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135°F or above  while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140(b) - Two large containers (several gallons) of chicken stock made this morning at 9a had internal temperatures of 61F and 65F at 315p. Chicken stock was discarded during inspection. Large metal bin used for ice bath was observed to contain more water than ice and needed to be replenished for recently prepared sauces and chopped garlic. Maintain ice baths to allow for proper/rapid cooling. Use several smaller containers to allow for rapid cooling, and then combine into a larger storage container once foods are properly cooled.
 
Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Monitor time and temperature of cooling foods to ensure benchmark temperatures are reached w/in designated time frames.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 -  Several packages of frozen shrimp and scallops were observed in a prep sink thawing. Standing water was surrounding containers, and only one container of frozen product had cold running water in direct contact with thawing seafood. Most of the seafood was labeled and placed in the walkin cooler. One container was left in the prep sink under cold running water until staff were ready to prep and label the items.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under potable running water 70F/below, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750.810b - A) Observed an empty sani-bucket at the tasting counter. Keep sani-buckets full and ready for use when in operation. 
B) Also, observed sani-buckets at the wait line and in prep area to be testing below proper concentration (100ppm quat or less). Buckets were refilled during inspection (200ppm Quat).

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) inside ice machine (black and pink mold around opening in ceiling where ice comes out);   and
B) hood baffles over cooking equipment (grease/dust).

Clean and sanitize the aforementioned food contact surfaces as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120e Facility has a number of soap dispensers that are not properly dispensing. A manager stated that replacement dispensers are available and awaiting install. In the meantime, dispensers at the bar and tasting counter were not properly dispensing. Bottles were unscrewed from the base making product available to staff. Paper towels were not available at the tasting counter handsink. Sink was supplied with towels during the inspection. Soap need only be available for handwashing - the style of dispenser is not a concern. Bar and tasting counter were not properly washing hands if soap was not available.

A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Grilled root vegetables prepped around 1p were observed in the bottom drawer of one of the cook line coolers. Internal temperature was 59F when checked around 3p. Normally grilled vegetables are cooled on a baking sheet in the walkin cooler. Today vegetables were placed directly in the drawer of the prep cooler after grilling. Management was advised time must be tracked during cooling process to ensure proper cooling of foods. Based on information provided plenty of time remained for product to reach 41F/below. Vegetables were pulled to be placed in walkin cooler to finish rapidly cooling.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
**Be careful with hot foods being placed in coolers - this can cause issues that may result in coolers and foods reaching temperatures above 41F and possibly compromise units and the food inside.**

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Butter based sauces in steam table had surface and internal temperatures of 110F-120F and 115F-128F. Sauces were double panned and were out for lunch service. Sauces were pulled from service and discarded. Current setup did not allow for sufficient heat transfer to maintain sauces at 135F/above. Management was advised to consider single pans or adding hot water to bottom pan if products will be double panned in steam table. 

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 140F/above  while on display and service.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed the sani-bucket in the wait area to be shallow and low concentration. During the inspection, the bucket was filled. Solution covered the cloth and tested at 200ppm Quat solution. Make sure staff knows to fill the sani-buckets to at least cloth level. Do not allow cloths to rest over the solution level. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee washed hands and shut off the manual faucet with paper towel as a barrier prior to drying hands. The same paper towel was then used to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employee re-washed hands with proper technique and dried hands prior to shutting off the manual faucet with a paper towel.
Make sure paper towel is used to dry hands prior to using as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet to avoid recontamination freshly washed hands.

Hands must be properly washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, between tasks as needed when hands have become contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Chlorine test kit was not available/in use at tasting bar. Chlorine test strips are needed to check sanitizer concentration for dish machine at both bars. Maintain chlorine test kits at both bars. Check the machines daily to ensure proper sanitizer concentration is maintained.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Vegetable slicer was going through manual ware washing at 3 part sink. After wash and rinse steps employee dunked the slicer in sanitizer compartment twice and then set it aside to air dry. Employee was advised food contact surfaces must be submerged for 60 seconds prior to setting aside to air dry. Slicer was placed back in sanitizer solution to finish properly sanitizing.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). For all items that can be physically taken to the 3 part sink for manual ware washing, equipment/utensils must be submerged for at least 60 seconds prior to setting aside to air dry.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 - A) SiLVERWARE WRAPPING AREA - Clean utensils were observed with food surfaces extended up out of storage bins.

B) BACK PREP - Clean spatulas and a whisk were observed with food surfaces extended up out of a pitcher used for storage.

Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be stored and handled in a way that protects them from contamination. All utensils shall be touched only by their handles and stored with handles presented out to avoid potential contamination of food contact surfaces when utensils are being retrieved.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text:
750.1310 - Bottles of Windex and Ecolab stainless steel polish were observed over pineapple juice, cranberry juice, and possible food containers at the bar. Chemical bottles were moved to proper storage area away from food and food related items.

All toxic items must be properly stored separate from food, clean equipment, and single service articles to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 280 - Paper cup was observed in bulk salt container in upstairs storage area. Cup was removed and discarded.

Suitable utensils shall be used when handling ready to eat foods to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.160, 510, 512, & 1120 - One employee changed gloves and did not wash hands between glove changes. Another employee was observed blowing inside a single use glove before putting the glove on his hand. An employee was also observed handling a wet cloth and appeared to be wiping gloved hands with wiping cloth. 
Proper use of gloves and handwashing were discussed at length during the inspection. Proper use of wiping cloths was also discussed.

Hands shall properly be washed (20 sec, soap/running water, paper towels to dry hands and then shut off manual faucet with paper towels) before handling food/clean equipment/unwrapped single service articles, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and  any time hands may have been contaminated.
Gloves are intended for one use and must be changed when torn, soiled, or there is an interruption in operations. Remove gloves immediately upon walking away from prep and discontinuing practice. Wash hands and put on a new pair of gloves before returning to task.
Common towels are prohibited. Do not use cloth towels, wet wiping cloths, or aprons to wipe hands.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Management was unable to locate test strips during the inspection. Quat test strips are needed for wall dispenser used to fill sani-buckets. Chlorine test strips are needed for the wine tasting room dish machine and the sanitizer used at the bar 3 part sink. Obtain and use test strips.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A) Bucket that tested at ~100ppm quat was used to wipe off a stem thermometer between uses. Thermometer was immediately cleaned and sanitized by manager.
NOTE: Separate sanitizer solutions must be used for food contact surfaces and non-food contact surfaces. Management has stem thermometer alcohol wipes. Management was also advised on manual wash, rinse, sanitize of stem thermometers up to every 4hrs.

B) Sanitizer solutions in a few buckets (i.e. server alley) tested at 0ppm quat. All were remade at proper concentration (150-200ppm; chemical range for sanitizer is 150-400ppm).
Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often is solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

C) Employee was observed walking around with wet wiping cloth in his hand. Employee noted it was for wiping surfaces but was not from a sanitizer solution. Employee was advised on proper use of wiping cloths, sanitizer solutions, and storage or wiping cloths between uses.
Use wiping cloths from sanitizer solutions for wiping surfaces, and store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 - A) Clean forks were observed with food surfaces extended up out of storage containers. Forks were placed back in dish area to go through ware washing process again.

B) Forks and spoons (shared utensils) in a tub at the server alley were observed with food contact surfaces and handles stored intermixed.

Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be stored and handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles and stored with handles presented out to avoid potential contamination of food contact surfaces when utensils are being retrieved.
